subject: DPA: log forwarding & cross-border retention questions

Subject: DPA: log forwarding & cross-border retention questions

Hi Jonas,

We're working through the DPA redlines with our legal & SecOps team and hit a few specific questions around log forwarding and retention that we need clarified before sign-off. Attached is a short list (ACME_DPA_LogQuestions.pdf) but the high-level items are:

- We plan to ingest Redwood service logs into our US-based SIEM. Some log fields may contain EU-sourced PII (user IDs, prompt snippets). Do you support field-level scrubbing/tokenization before forwarding, or a routing option that keeps EU-origin logs in-region?
- Retention: We need a contractual guarantee for onshore retention of forwarded logs (30/90/365 day options). What retention controls and SLA for deletion can you put in the DPA?
- Backups/snapshots: Are forwarded logs included in cross-region backups? If so, what's the deletion/erase process for backups and timelines for certification of erasure?
- Lawful access & keys: Can forwarding be encrypted with our KMS keys (BYOK) so Redwood cannot decrypt?

Can you provide suggested DPA language and any operational playbook we can hand to our Security Ops team? We're aiming to close this week; happy to set a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Asha Mehra
Senior Counsel, Data Protection - Acme Corp
acme dpa team

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: DPA: log forwarding & cross-border retention questions

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list. Short answers and an ops summary attached (redwood-log-handling-summary.pdf). Longer notes below.

1) Field-level filtering / tokenization: we support an ingestion pipeline that can redact or hash specified fields prior to forwarding. For high-risk fields (prompt text, free-text responses) we recommend tokenization at collection time; we can provide a webhook-based pre-forwarding transform or a managed tokenization option.

2) Retention windows: contract controls we can offer: a default 30-day onshore retention for forwarded logs, optional 90/365 day tiers with commercial addendum. Deletion SLA for forwarded logs is 72 hours for active indices; backup/snapshot erasure follows the backup schedule (see below). We'll propose specific DPA language for the retention clause.

3) Backups & snapshots: forwarded logs may be included in encrypted snapshots depending on your chosen routing. Snapshots are immutable for their TTL; operationally, we maintain a documented restore-and-purge process that allows us to certify erasure from backups within 14 days of a request where feasible. For EU-origin data you can choose a geofenced route that avoids cross-border snapshot replication.

4) BYOK / lawful access: we support customer-managed keying for log-forwarding channels (TLS+client cert + optional envelope encryption with customer KMS). However, some managed operational workflows (indexing, anonymization) require readable data; we can architect a flow where the raw forwarded stream is encrypted at-rest with your KMS and only decrypted into a customer-controlled SIEM endpoint. We'll call this out in redlines.

Next steps: I'm attaching a 1-page summary and a proposed redline snippet (I will follow up with the .docx). Can we do a 30-min call Thurs 11/2 09:00 PST to walk the SecOps playbook?

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-log-handling-summary.pdf (2 pages)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: log forwarding & cross-border retention questions

Asha / team — quick operational clarifications from our side to supplement Jonas's notes:

- Routing: For EU-origin data we can enable an onshore-forwarding-only path. That option prevents cross-border replication and excludes those records from cross-region snapshots by tagging records at ingestion.
- Default backups: standard retention for snapshots is 30 days (configurable). We can carve out forwarded-SIEM exports from snapshot replication entirely if you want a strict onshore-only policy.
- Erasure certification: we can provide a signed operational certificate that lists steps taken (index deletion, tombstone, snapshot purge, metadata prune) and timing. Our usual window for cert issuance is 10 business days.
- BYOK: we can support envelope encryption with customer KMS for the forwarding channel. For usability we recommend a short-lived key rotation policy (30 days).

I'm attaching our proposed redline language as a starting point (redwood-proposed-redlines.docx). Two notes to watch for in the DPA: (1) how we define \"forwarded logs\" vs. \"service telemetry\" (we suggest explicit field definitions), and (2) a practical exception for lawful access requests served to Redwood that require limited disclosure to our ops team for incident response; we can keep that narrow and auditable.

If this looks acceptable, Jonas and I can incorporate your comments into a single DPA addendum and circulate.

—Marissa

Thanks Marissa & Jonas — the summaries are helpful. A couple of asks from our side before we redline formally:

1) Please add explicit language that forwarded logs containing EU-sourced personal data will not be replicated to non-EEA backups unless we opt in in writing.
2) Please include the 10-business-day erasure certification timeline as a firm SLA in the addendum.

If you can incorporate those two items we should be able to circulate a one-way redline for signature. Also please send the DocuSign link when you have the final addendum ready.

Kind regards,
Samir Patel
Security Operations — Acme Corp
securityops@acme.com
